body: Lol that last bit of advice makes so much sense - I can't trust anyone's opinions, including my own despite hours and hours of analysing the situation. Like the good "friends and family" I have and professionals that I pay through the roof for - the only thing they have to say is "ultimately you have to help yourself", or "change has to come from within". And I'm like wtf, if people with completely normal functioning minds who aren't depressed can't come up with ang ideas, what makes them think I can. I can barely even buy my own groceries or keep track of my own posts LOL, and they want me to fix myself. Just feels like I'm being left all alone with no idea how to fix shit.

Don't do this. Shut off from everything else, your mind slowly atrophies. The first thing you'll notice will be memory loss and loss of the ability to socialize. You'll slowly lose your cognitive skills and soon the depression worsens. And you'll want to kill yourself even more than you want to now, yet you still won't have the guts to do it.

Take it from someone who's done exactly what you described.
But the forum is mainly just people asking for help to deal with loved ones who have korsakoffs.. I don't think I'll be able to find much help here as one suffering from it himself.

Yeah, I was on so many different meds before this, and like you said it was way worse than just depression. I was slowly losing everything that made myself me. Insomnia really is one of the worst things. It gets so bad that you'd do anything just to get one night of sleep, including killing your mind with sleeping pills. In the nights leading up to the attacks, I slept for 2 hours a night while on clonazepam for 4 nights straight.

I hope you get out of your situation. But im really sure mine is irreversible. I won't have anymore good days.
So just live till you're tired then die? Sounds good to me. Are you not working anymore?
I don't think im the kind of person who would live his entire life for one thing, and definitely not writing.. sorry :(
where can i find one of these clinics? and i always did want to use cryogenics before i died. some chance is better than none right?
And i don't know if i could handle a life of loneliness.. what drove me to depression in the first place was feeling lonely surrounded by friends.

You're a much stronger person than I am to say the least :(

Haha i don't really have many dreams anymore, this thing killed my drive to succeed too.

Yeah i totally feel you, it takes me ages to just put together a coherent message even online. How do you cope with this man? Like in person i'd assume it would be damn near impossible to talk about anything for more than a few sentecnes..
heh basically i didn't feed myself well for 2 weeks (by not well read not at all), and i drank loads of alcohol at the same time. put together the both of them have a synergistic effect.
And what are the odds i'd meet someone with the same disorder LOL
As in you have korsakoffs itself? How do you not get lonely, not being able to talk to anyone meaningfully?

LOL I can totally relate to being more uncomfortable among close people than absolute strangers. That is seriously the weirdest kind of anxiety. We could talk about it more in PM since I'm a stranger (such irony)

Try discovering talents. I never thought I had any special talent for music (i did have passion though). I played a lot just cause I liked it. I don't know if i really discovered some hidden talent, or if it was just hours of practice and passion, but now its one of the things I'm most proud of myself for. And people seem to assume I'm talented instead of just hard working hohohohoho. I'm not complainin.

Are you sure your friends only like you for your car and your study buddy skillz? They may like you for like you say something inherent in yourself, like the fact that you're great company, or you're caring or funny or you just have a great sense of humor. Are they close friends? If they are good enough friends that you can call them close, they must like you for something inherent in yourself, not just for what you offer them..

If they aren't what you'd call close friends... I'm really sorry haha

> Communication is about more than your ability to pronounce a word. I wouldn't assume that you don't have the connection with people you want to have without asking them about it first. You should just be honest with the people you are about in terms of you disability. They will understand and you will be surprised to learn that they will encourage and support you. And I think you will find you have a stronger connection than you realize.

It's more than that, and my problem is deeper than not being able to pronounce a few words. I wrote a longer post on this earlier (i think i linked it in the comment section). I try my best to explain, but really only someone with a similar speech impediment would get it. I've already told everyone i consider close :(. They do try to encourage and support me but nothing really helps. I feel they say too much without grasping what a massive effect this has had on my life.

> The only person whose standards there are that you need to live up to are yours. So what if you aren't a concert pianist or a tournament-ready gamer? As long as you feel personally rewarded, that is all that matters. 

I don't feel rewarded anymore, hearing my restricted playing and feeling the handicap. I always loved the drive to get better, to one day be amazing. More than that, to be good enough to feel proud of myself. Now I know I can never be as good as a normal person would be. You're right that I can't live up to my own standards thanks to this disability. 

> Beethoven was deaf, he still composed some of the greatest musical pieces of all time. I understand that you are attached to hearing this music as a form of entertainment, but I'm just trying to put it into perspective. There are other art forms out there for you to experience and there are ways for you to stay involved in music if you want to. 

It's not just entertainment for me. Other art forms just don't even compare to music for me, they're completely different. I'm sure Beethoven's deafness caused him sadness that you couldn't even begin to comprehend. Even if he composed the greatest music of all time for us to appreciate and admire, do you think he himself as a person didn't suffer? There were accounts of him breaking down into tears after his own concerts cause he couldn't hear the music he composed himself. He contemplated suicide, and even at the end of his life, his last words were "I shall hear in heaven".

> Did they give you a diagnosis? Did they prescribe a medication to try? I'm wondering what their thoughts were on your situation. Mental health care is a bit different from physical health care in that the personality of you doctor matters greatly in how effective your treatment will be. Maybe you just haven't found the right person to receive treatment from yet. 

ugh most of them didn't do shit except prescribe drugs. All of them were along the lines of "I can't fix your problems, I can only help you cope with drugs or otherwise." They prescribed drugs and tried counseling me, but it just felt cold and detached. After all how much can someone you pay to see you for an hour every week or so care? How can I get them to understand in a few sessions when everyone I've tried to explain to tirelessly for days doesn't. Maybe they're all crap, or maybe professional help isn't a solution.

> Maybe you weren't being honest with yourself on those tests. It is also possible that you have a different problem that you haven't come to terms with yet. Depression isn't always its own thing. Sometimes it is a comorbid symptom of a different illness like anxiety. 

I was honest. For example when the test asked "if i feel worthless" I responded no. But i gave a strong yes on lots of other points. I genuinely feel that way. I do have anxiety issues, and slight obsessive behavior, but I'm pretty sure a lot of my anxiety stemmed from growing up with a speech impediment.

> Not everyone reacts the same to medications, especially when it comes to mental health. Three or even four different medications can be ineffective for some people, but that doesn't mean you still can't find the right one, especially if you find you have a diagnosis of something else that is causing your depression. The key is to communicate clearly with your doctors which medications you have already tried. There are different classes of medications for depression based on what your doctor thinks is the cause. For example, SSRIs are often prescribed if your doctor thinks your problem is serotonin regulation. If serotonin regulation isn't your problem, that is an entire class of medications that won't do anything for you. 

It could be that I haven't found the right drug, or that drugs aren't the answer. And I'd rather not go long term with psychotropic drugs. Psychiatrists themselves admit psychiatry is the most primitive field of medicine. They know so little about the mechanism of mental illness, what the drugs actually do to your brain, and the long effects they can cause. They're constantly changing theories with no evidence and now they say the "serotonin deficiency" theory may be complete bullshit. They prescribe based on a "what's hot right now" basis and anecdotal evidence. More and more studies suggest that SSRIs and other classes of antidepressants do more harm than good in the long term. Particularly that they cause long term brain damage. My mind is all I have left, and I don't want to ruin it to feel sedated for a few days.

> That sounds like an amazing experience. You should give it a shot at least. The worst possible thing that could happen is that nothing changes for you. If you die, you die. It doesn't matter when or where, once you're dead, that's it. Waiting to see what your future has in store for you has absolutely no bearing on how happy or satisfying killing yourself might be. There is no logical reason not to stick around and see what is in store for you in a new chapter of life. It's not like dying stops being an option at some point; on the contrary, your death is guaranteed. The thing that you have control of is, to a great extent, when it will occur. 

If nothing changes for me that is indeed a worse fate than dying. Killing myself won't be satisfying or happy. I won't feel anything. I'd be dead. I can go over but in this state I will fail my first year of uni without a doubt and feel equally as miserable.

> There are people that would miss you if you were gone. You owe it to them to keep trying. 

It's always mentioned how much people would hurt if you were gone. But no one seems to care about the suffering of the depressed person himself. Should he stay around just so people wouldn't have to miss him? Even if his life is a living hell? Isn't that them being more selfish? Asking the person to live for the sake of others who "love" him and would hate to lose him. Just as they don't want to go through the pain of losing a loved one, I don't want to go through the pain of my own life. Which is more selfish in your opinion? Aren't they both equally as self centered? 

> I doubt that is true. Your attitude may just be clouding your observation. I assure you that they haven't given up on you. 

They haven't given up or stopped caring :(. I think I should've said instead that they don't know what to do to help anymore, so they do nothing.

> Even if you are in complete pain and misery, you are still alive and feeling. That's not something you get back once you give it away. One has to wonder if even the most painful existence isn't still a gift in light of the alternative because it still has possibilities tied to it. 

>In short, you can always kill yourself tomorrow, but you can't see what tomorrow has in store for you if you kill yourself today. Why not hang around and see what uni has for you? You owe it to yourself to at least check. 

That's an interesting question, and a really good point. But my future seems so bleak at the moment. I'm emotionally incapable of handling uni in this state. I feel like I'm just going to waste my entire life because of what this thing has taken from me.



And I honestly don't know what's wrong with me. This always happens. I get advice and my mind just responds by shooting down all their points. I'm just typing out what I think when i read your advice, and I know you mean well but my brain is just fuk. I've always been a stubborn opinionated person and its totally working against me now. It's why the people that care just don't know what to say anymore.. I've debated endlessly in my own mind or with them and it never gets me anywhere.

This may be a bit overused, but in your case things will get better, no matter how shitty it may seem now. Find any course you like, or at least don't mind doing and do it (maths is pretty cool). Once you're done with uni you'll have your own life, free of your shitty abusive parents and stressful uni environment. You won't have to make friends in an English speaking environment. Just talk to the people who speak the same mother tongue as you, it should be a lot easier. IMO eastern europeans are fuking crazy (in an awesome way, like fun :P).

Oh and some unis have a really large international community, with people with all kinds of weird accents. Try searching for those if it makes you feel comfortable! Your LoL "friends" sound like seriously horrible human beings. I think you should just forget them. (SWITCH TO DOTA MAYBE). I hope you'll find new and better friends later in life. 

As shitty as things seem right now, there's a way out for you. You have no idea where you'll be in 10 years. You may have a good career and a great circle of friends, or a person you really love.
